key_insight: AlgoRAG shows that retrieval-augmented generation can deliver accurate, pedagogically useful explanations for abstract theoretical computer science topics by combining an LLM with a curated domain knowledge base.
engineering_relevance: The paper demonstrates a practical blueprint for building domain-specialized AI tutors for proof-heavy STEM subjects using notation-aware retrieval, entity recognition, and pedagogical ranking.
method: Curated knowledge base: textbooks, lecture slides, practice problems, proof templates, and worksheets
Domain-specific retrieval: mathematical entity recognition and notation-aware search
Pedagogical re-ranking to improve explanation quality and instructional usefulness
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 179 exam-style questions across core TCS topics, AlgoRAG achieved 100% success with mean response time of 38.0 seconds and strong pedagogical quality despite low n-gram overlap metrics.
watch_item: BLEU-4 was zero and ROUGE scores were modest, so automatic text-similarity metrics may understate correctness; results also depend on a carefully curated domain corpus and evaluation set.
paper_title: AlgoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Theoretical Computer Science Education -- A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Theory
